title: Cloud Connector provisioning URLs on the wire: what the template sets, VM size and cloud provider fields

prose.text: A cloud provisioning URL carries what a new Cloud Connector VM needs to enroll: the cloud provider, location and group settings, and the VM size. The provisioning URL paths and SDK methods are generated; this subject maps the console template to the API fields.

{{url-prerequisite}} {{same-url-per-vpc}} The autoscaling and non-autoscaling templates must match the deployment, [[cloud-connector.overview.groups:template-match]], and autoscaling is enabled only through Zscaler Support, [[cloud-connector.azure.vmss:support-gated]].
{{template-vm-size}} {{contract-form-factor}} {{clients-form-factor}} {{vm-size-is-form-factor}} How the size pairs with an EC2 instance type is in [[cloud-connector.aws.instance-sizing]].
The contract's cloud provider list omits GCP, which the console template and the Terraform provider offer {{divergence:cloud-provider-type}}.

{{python-crud-1-9-13}} The Go provisioning URL functions use the generic (ZIA-routed) client methods, which fail in the provider's legacy mode: [[cloud-connector.sdk-go.service-defects:legacy-ztw-only-client-fails-generic-calls]].

checks.do: Whether the provisioning URL a deployment uses carries the VM size (form factor) the deployment expects, since the size is set in the template, not in the cloud template alone.
For a GCP provisioning URL written through the raw API, whether the API accepts a cloud provider value the contract does not list.

url-prerequisite.statement: The cloud provisioning URL is a prerequisite for deploying Cloud Connector as a VM in AWS, Azure and GCP, and is obtained by configuring a provisioning template; the same URL can be used multiple times.

quotes: The cloud provisioning URL is a prerequisite for deploying the Cloud Connector as a virtual machine (VM) in Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). To obtain a provisioning URL, you must configure the provisioning template.
Use the same provisioning URL multiple times based on your requirements.

same-url-per-vpc.statement: Cloud Connector VMs deployed in a single VPC must use the same provisioning URL.

quotes: You must use the same provisioning URL for the Cloud Connector VMs deployed in a single Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

template-vm-size.statement: In the template's group settings the VM size depends on the cloud: AWS offers Small, Medium or Large, with Small set by default when autoscaling is enabled; Azure and GCP are set to Small by default.

quotes: VM Size: Depending on your selected cloud provider, you can configure your Cloud Connector VM size.
Amazon Web Services: Select from Small, Medium, or Large. Small is set by default when autoscaling is enabled.
Azure: Small is set by default.
GCP: Small is set by default.

contract-form-factor.statement: The contract's provisioning URL content (`provUrlData`) has a `formFactor` field with the values `SMALL`, `MEDIUM` and `LARGE`.

expect.description: Form factor of Cloud & Branch Connector provisioning URL.

clients-form-factor.statement: The Go SDK's provisioning URL data model (`ProvUrlData`) carries `FormFactor` as a string, and the ZTC provider's `form_factor` accepts `SMALL`, `MEDIUM` or `LARGE`.

quotes: "form_factor": { Type: schema.TypeString, Optional: true, Computed: true, ValidateFunc: validation.StringInSlice([]string{ "SMALL", "MEDIUM", "LARGE", }, false), },

vm-size-is-form-factor.statement: So the console's VM Size is carried in the API as the provisioning URL's `formFactor`, not in a field named for VM size.
vm-size-is-form-factor.conditions: The legacy API reference describes a VM's formFactor as its size; that the console's VM Size label is this field rests on the matching names and that description, not on a source naming the console label.

expect.description: The form factor size of the VM. The supported values are SAMLL, MEDIUM, or LARGE.

python-crud-1-9-13.statement: The Python SDK added create, read, update and delete functions for the ZTW provisioning URL in release 1.9.13 (PR #450).

quotes: [PR #450](https://github.com/zscaler/zscaler-sdk-python/pull/450) - Added new CRUD functioins for ZTW `provisioning_url` resource api.

cloud-provider-type.summary: Whether a provisioning URL's cloud provider can be GCP.

quotes: "cloud_provider_type": { Type: schema.TypeString, Optional: true, Computed: true, ValidateFunc: validation.StringInSlice([]string{ "AWS", "AZURE", "GCP", }, false), },

positions.says: The console template offers Amazon Web Services, Azure or Google Cloud as the cloud provider.

quotes: On the Cloud Provider tab, select Amazon Web Services, Azure, or Google Cloud as the cloud provider for which you want to deploy the Cloud Connector.

cloud-provider-type.impact: The contract's enum looks out of date for GCP; GCP provisioning URLs exist in the console and the provider. Code that validates against the contract enum would reject a GCP template.
